purpose: Closed vocabularies for the review-findings ledger (PILOT P0-1, ADVISORY-RSI-2026-08-27-v4 §5). One machine-readable source shared by every writer (hooks/verdict-contract.sh, skills/retro/scripts/itd_review_import.py) and by the reader (skills/retro/scripts/itd_retro_scan.py). Validation is forward-only: records written before taxonomy_version 1 are never rewritten, they are normalized on read through legacyMapping.

meaning.subagent-verdict: A review subagent's own machine-readable verdict, persisted by hooks/verdict-contract.sh.
meaning.external-github-review: A GitHub PR review comment normalized by skills/retro/scripts/itd_review_import.py.
meaning.manual-entry: A record appended by hand or by a one-off script; the writer must still name a lineage.

severity.note: unspecified means 'the writer could not grade it', not a grade. A review subagent always grades its own findings, so unspecified is invalid for subagent-verdict.

meaning.correctness: The code does the wrong thing: bad logic, wrong order, wrong predicate, wrong serialization.
meaning.incomplete-fix: The change does not close what it claims to close; part of the stated subject is left undone.
meaning.test-coverage: A guarantee is unproven: no test, no mutation, or the test cannot fail.
meaning.documentation-accuracy: Docs, comments or contracts disagree with the code they describe.
meaning.unsupported-claim: A claim is stronger than its evidence (a PASSED without a receipt, a count without a measurement).
meaning.swallowed-diagnostic: An error, a failure or a refusal is lost silently instead of being named.
meaning.over-inclusive-input: Input, scope or a match is wider than needed: over-broad regex, unbounded read, extra files.
meaning.duplication: The same logic exists in two places and can drift apart.
meaning.dead-code: Code, a rule or a branch that nothing can reach or that nothing consumes.
meaning.naming-collision: Two things claim one identifier: ADR numbers, migration numbers, ids, paths.
meaning.readability: Structure or naming makes the code harder to follow than it needs to be.
meaning.performance: Avoidable slowness or resource cost: missing index, seq scan, N+1, unbounded loop.
meaning.security: Secret exposure, missing authorization, injection, unsafe path, weakened gate.
meaning.unclassified: The writer is not a reviewer and did not classify the text (an imported external comment). Never valid for subagent-verdict: a review subagent classifies its own finding.

category.note: values — словарь ревьюера (13). bySource добавляет unclassified тем писателям, которые физически не выносят суждение о чужом тексте; это честная пометка «не классифицировано», а не лазейка для ревьюера.

legacyMapping.note: Applied on READ to records without taxonomy_version. Never rewrites the ledger.

rejection.note: A record that fails validation is NOT dropped and NOT admitted to the canonical ledger: it is appended here with the reason, and the counter file records how often each reason fired. The quarantine is the measured evidence for a taxonomy_version 2 rename/split/merge. The quarantine keeps every rejected record whole and never truncates one; the FILE is bounded by rotation into numbered generations, exactly like the canonical ledger. A repeated rejection of the same record for the same reason classes is skipped before the write when a previous entry is visible, but that check is a read-then-append and cannot be exact under concurrent writers. The MEASUREMENT is exact by construction instead: the counter is aggregated by distinct record identity, so the same rejection counts once no matter how many writers recorded it. Nothing is ever lost; at worst a duplicate line appears, bounded by rotation.

limits.note: A record larger than maxRecordBytes is not admitted to the canonical ledger: reason record:too-large. The quarantine still stores it IN FULL - the two requirements (a bounded ledger, a rejected record kept whole) are not in conflict, because the quarantine file is bounded by ROTATION, not by truncating a record. Rotation preserves; truncation destroys.
